incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on /v1/stream (hosted-prod). Metric spike started at 2024-06-15T20:04:16Z. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/services/streaming/p99?from=now-15m

alex (oncall): Acknowledged. Paging in SRE + runtime. Anyone seeing error spikes or customer reports?

maya (sre): I'm on it. Quick snapshot: p95 ~ 240ms -> 2600ms, p99 ~ 1.2s -> 18s over last 10m. Error rate for streaming chunk timeouts (upstream_read_timeout) up ~ 0.8%.

liam (runtime): I'm pulling proxy logs. Early hint: lots of upstream read timeouts and repeated small-chunk flushes. Example from nginx access/error log:

```
2024/06/15 20:03:58 [error] 12345#0: *98765 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api.redwood.internal, request: "GET /v1/stream?session=abc..." upstream: "http://10.5.6.7:8080/stream", host: "api.redwood.internal"
2024/06/15 20:04:01 [info] 12345#0: *98768 client closed connection, client: 10.2.3.9, server: api.redwood.internal, request: "GET /v1/stream?..."
```

liam (runtime): Also seeing runtime logs where kv-cache flushes coincide with big stalls: runtime/runtime.go:sendChunk flush duration=12034ms chunk_bytes=0

alex (oncall): Customer impact? jenny from CS?

jenny (cs): We've received three tickets flagged as "streaming stopped mid-response" from two customers on hosted. They reported the UI showing "loading" for 20-30s and then reconnect. No data loss reported yet but UX breaks. Customers: AcmeApp, DataDeck. Both on high-concurrency plans.

maya (sre): Hypothesis: client backpressure + proxy buffering causing upstream to hold onto chunks -> large tail latency when downstream finally reads. Nginx default proxy_buffering may coalesce chunks; when combined with long-running keepalives or upstream GC we get big tail spikes. Also seeing an increase in keepalive resets.

liam (runtime): Runtime hypothesis: we recently landed a micro-optimization that batches small tokens into fewer flushes under high load to reduce syscalls. That reduces throughput but increases latency under backpressure. Reverting or lowering that threshold might help.

alex (oncall): Mitigation plan (short):
- Turn OFF proxy_buffering for /v1/stream path in edge proxy for hosted-prod (nginx conf).
- Increase upstream_read_timeout from 30s -> 60s to avoid early 504s while we validate.
- Roll a canary of runtime patch that forces flush interval to 50ms (was 200ms) for streaming sessions.
- Rate-limit long-lived streams per token to reduce noisy neighbors.

incidents-bot: ACTION CREATED: #INC-17491 - apply nginx streaming buffer changes in prod-edge (priority P1).

maya (sre): Applying proxy_buffering=off in staged edge pool now to canary nodes (2/10). Monitoring for chunk flow.

liam (runtime): Preparing quick revert of batching change; can push a 1-line config to lower the coalescing window. Ready to deploy once proxies stable.

20:12:40 alex (oncall): Canary proxy change rolled to 2 nodes: initial effect looks promising. p99 on those nodes back down to ~900ms vs 12s before. No new errors in canary logs.

20:17:04 maya (sre): Rolling proxy change to remaining nodes with gradual throttle (30s per node). Setting incident channel to urgent if any node shows >5s p99.

20:22:11 liam (runtime): Deployed runtime config change (flush interval 50ms) to 10% of streaming pool. Early signal: chunk latencies on those hosts dropped 3x, client-side rebuffer events reduced.

20:28:03 maya (sre): Full proxy rollout complete. Cluster p99 back to baseline ~300-400ms. Error rates (upstream_read_timeout) dropped from 0.8% -> 0.04%.

20:31:45 jenny (cs): Sent interim update to affected customers summarizing mitigations: proxy config change + runtime flush adjustment. Noted we'll follow up with RCA. Customers acknowledged and flagged for post-incident review.

20:38:10 alex (oncall): Handoff summary for night oncall (noah):
- Incident: p99 tail latency on /v1/stream (hosted-prod) due to chunk coalescing + client backpressure + proxy buffering.
- Actions taken: proxy_buffering=off on streaming path, upstream_read_timeout increased to 60s, runtime flush interval reduced to 50ms on canary -> rolled to pool. Rate-limits added as temporary mitigations.
- Current state: p99 stabilized, error rate ~0.04%, customer-impact tickets open but degraded UX resolved.
- Next steps: create postmortem, revert upstream_read_timeout to default after confidence window, add automated test for streaming backpressure, consider persistent proxy config for streaming endpoints, track runtime coalescing feature in feature flag.

noah (oncall-night): Acknowledged. I'll watch alerts for next 4h and escalate if recurrence. Please add me to postmortem when created.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to SEV-2. Create postmortem doc: /wiki/incidents/INC-17491-postmortem

alex (oncall): Closing handoff. One action for engineering: liam to open PR to add a streaming load test that simulates slow clients/backpressure. jenny to bundle customer logs for RCA.

liam (runtime): Will open PR with test harness today and include metrics for flush intervals, chunk sizes, and client-read-sleep simulation.

jenny (cs): I'll collect support threads and attach timestamps + session ids.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99 returned to baseline at 2024-06-15T20:35:56Z. Follow-up tasks assigned.

alex (oncall): Thanks team. Filing for postmortem.
